Listen, if you're seeing this, and you have your doubts due the price, or the mixed reviews, that's okay.
I'll just say my two bits... This game is EARLY ACCESS. Of course it's going through it's growing pains. You aren't buying a finished product, you're buying an opportunity to guide a game to the success it deserves. You, yes YOU can see what the game's like, can GIVE FEEDBACK, and can TELL THEM WHAT YOU WANT TO SEE.
Game too hard? Tell them. Game too easy? Tell them. Game too boring? Tell them.
This is a child.
Foster it.

One big problem for players coming from DRG "Standard" is that the Corespawn are functionally very different from the Glyphids, so you cannot treat them the same way. The biggest problem is that the standard enemies frequently leap around, and are very rarely packed together like the Glyphids do.

Once you get past that, it is a very fun game! Build variety mostly just comes down to your weapons, however, and perks are just to amplify what you can do for the most part.

Yeah I don't recommend this game at it's current state. The gist of it being already laid out by other reviewers. 

[list]
   [*]The meta-progression is super boring and doesn't feel good to grind for. The bio booster decks is not a fun mechanic to play around since the build choice and only being given two options in a run gets repetitive quick. The enhancements feels awful to spend on, especially since every character have the same ones but you need to grind for each of them separately.
   [*]The weapon upgrades are lackluster and you get so few of them and the you never feel like you scale unless you get exceptionally lucky.
   [*]Some character upgrades in runs are fun, but many of them are so underbaked or niche it would never be good to pick them. 
   [*]Extra objectives only being cameras and terminals is dumb and it doesn't give you anything except credit boosts. 
   [*]Both weapon and character cosmetics being either non-existent or dull.
   [*]Rarely get a feeling of clutching a victory, dopamine from a busted run and more often feeling powerless because you got shafted by lame upgrades. 

The foundation is there (largely because it's has the original DRG as it's base, but I digress) but multiple core systems needs to be overhauled, redesigned or improved for it to have any legs worth standing in the long term. 

Even reading to Update 2, I didn't feel any excitement going back in (with the exception being that they finally removed the movement speed penalty from heavy attack kills, why it even had one to begin with for that long is insanity to me)

This game is objectively inferior to its predecessor, with far less emphasis on co-operative gameplay. The Corespawn enemies are often frustrating to fight and are more computationally expensive than their Glyphid counterparts, meaning you will dramatically lose performance as the game progresses.

The development team has failed to show any serious effort in bettering this game because they actively resist making compromises in their creative vision. They squandered all of their time with their Alpha access builds, refusing to listen to valid criticisms, then went on vacation immediately after releasing this game as an Early Access title. They are extremely slow in their efforts to make critical and necessary changes, instead allowing the playerbase to plummet and continue to drop (as of the time of this review, only up to ~500 daily users are logged on Steam.)

The development team has constantly made unwanted and unasked for changes such as arbitrary invincibility phases upon dealing too much damage to a boss. It takes months to finally concede and remove actively harmful features such as the aforementioned invincibility phases or the requirement for all players to stand near ELLIS to pick an upgrade (which substantially sabotaged the flow of gameplay). Some unpopular features, such as the Reaperworms (essentially invincible Leeches from DRG) are yet to be reworked or removed.

Terrain generation is objectively worse in every possible facet, compared to DRG. This was yet another primary appeal to DRG, which featured likely tens of thousands, if not hundreds of thousands, of possible procedurally generated caves, often featuring non-linear expanses that varied in depth and complexity. Rogue Core does not have this selling point. It essentially takes only one method of cave generation (that of Mining Expedition), and repeats it ad-nauseum with a few Expenite events (which are basically just Core Infuser events from DRG) littered about. There are few mining structures from the DRG company sprinkled throughout, but these are hardly enough to compensate for the extremely thin variety in cave generations.

Finally, this game lacks any meaningful sense of progression beyond the rather small amount of achievements to collect. While the lack of cosmetics relative to DRG could be justified (and arguably excused), many of the cosmetics carried over from the preceding game are locked behind cosmetic crates (basically the Cargo Crates and Lost Gear minus the tasks of recovering batteries or recovering the gear). These crates require an extreme investment of time, as they only have a chance to spawn. Not much more can be said of this beyond hope that the developers will move these cosmetics into a more respectful progression system, as they had done with DRG's (formerly) retired seasons. 

In short, this game needs a lot of work to be worth the price tag it is now. This is work that the developers have consistently failed to show they are willing to do, and thus, at the current rate, it will take several years (if not a decade or two) to present a polished product that is just as extraordinary as their lightning-in-a-bottle game Deep Rock Galactic. Therefore, this game is deserving of a negative review until the developers demonstrate their intent to refine this game into what it should be: a worthy counterpart to Deep Rock Galactic.
